newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bond prices seen stable at Wednesday sale.
newsitem.headline: Russian bond prices seen stable at Wednesday sale.

text.p: Primary dealers's funds alone will keep Russian OFZ interest-bearing bonds prices stable at Wednesday's auctions as issue volumes are low, dealers said on Tuesday.
ON WEDNESDAY
THE FINANCE MINISTRY SELLS:
*4.00 trln rbls in an addtional 686-day bond tranche (series 24013)
*2 trls rbls in an additional 1,067-day bond tranche (series 25016)
THE FINANCE MINISTRY PAYS/REPAYS
*3.30 trln rbls in maturing 18-month bond (series 24005) and 354.39 bln rbls in interest on the bond
ON TUESDAY
*Average yield fell to 18.0 pct from 18.4 pct on Monday
*Turnover rose to 3.83 trln rbls from 2.69 trln rbls
*Central bank sold 695.30 bln rbls of bills, bonds
*Series 25016 bond closed at 100.89 to yield 19.51 pct
*Series 24013 bond closed at 101.35 to yield 22.17 pct
ABN-Amro fixed income dealer Andrei Babenko said that given the small issue and repayment volumes funds from primary dealers alone would be enough to keep prices at current market levels.
"Any bids at lower prices will be cut off," he said.
Primary dealers must put at least some of their bids at non-competitive levels, which are satisfied automatically. There are 44 primary dealers in Russia.
Babenko said non-residents's bids would have little impact on the results of the auctions, as their limits for the sales were small.
He said foreingers started buying long-term paper at secondary trading pushing prices higher by about 20 basis points.
Yields have recently fallen to about 19 percent from 30 percent in May and CS First Boston dealer Sergei Koshelenko forecast a further fall in the yields.
"Russian investors think the yields will go down even further," he said.
--Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
